title.raw: 卷24 志第19 食貨 Volume 24 Treatises 19: Finance and Economics

sentences.zh: 王者量地以制邑，度地以居人，總土地所生，料山澤之利，式遵行令，敬授人時，農商趣向，各本事業。

translations.literal: The king measures land to establish settlements, gauges land to settle people, totals what the land produces, estimates the profit of mountains and marshes, reverently follows and implements orders, respectfully grants the seasons to the people, farmers and merchants hasten toward their pursuits, each attending to his own occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign measures land to lay out towns, assesses terrain to settle the people, tallies what the soil yields, estimates the bounty of hills and marshes, reverently upholds and enforces the laws, dutifully grants the seasons to the people, and farmers and merchants each pursue their calling according to their trade.

sentences.zh: 書稱懋遷有無，言穀貨流通，咸得其所者也。

translations.literal: The Documents say 'diligently move what is lacking and what is abundant,' meaning grain and goods circulate and all obtain their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents speaks of 'diligently moving abundance to where there is want'—that is, grain and goods circulate so that each reaches its proper place.

sentences.zh: 周官太府，掌九貢九賦之法，王之經用，各有等差。

translations.literal: In the Offices of Zhou, the Grand Steward managed the methods of the nine tributes and nine levies; the king's regular expenditures each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Steward oversaw the methods of the nine tributes and nine levies; the king's routine expenditures were graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 所謂取之以道，用之有節，故能養百官之政，勗戰士之功，救天災，服方外，活國安人之大經也。

translations.literal: What is called taking by the Way and using with restraint—thus one can sustain the governance of the hundred officials, encourage the merit of warriors, relieve heavenly disasters, subdue the outer regions, and preserve the state and settle the people—the great constant of governance.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by taking through proper means and spending with restraint: only thus can one sustain the administration of officials, reward the achievements of soldiers, relieve natural disasters, bring distant lands to submission, and preserve the state and secure the people—the great principle of governance.

sentences.zh: 爰自軒、頊，至于堯、舜，皆因其所利而勸之，因其所欲而化之。

translations.literal: From Xuanyuan and Zhuanxu down to Yao and Shun, all encouraged them according to what benefited them and transformed them according to what they desired.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor and Zhuanxu down to Yao and Shun, each ruler encouraged the people through what benefited them and transformed them through what they desired.

sentences.zh: 不奪其時，不窮其力，輕其征，薄其賦，此五帝三皇不易之教也。

translations.literal: Not seizing their seasons, not exhausting their strength, lightening their levies, reducing their taxes—this is the teaching of the Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns that never changes.
translations.idiomatic: Not seizing their seasons, not exhausting their strength, lightening levies, and reducing taxes—this is the unchanging teaching of the Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 古語曰：「善為人者，愛其力而成其財。

translations.literal: An ancient saying says: 'One who is good at governing others cherishes their strength and completes their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: An old saying runs: 'A good ruler cherishes the people's strength and builds up their wealth.

sentences.zh: 」若使之不以道，斂之如不及，財盡則怨，力盡則叛。

translations.literal: ' If one employs them not by the Way, and collects as though unable to catch up, when wealth is exhausted there is resentment; when strength is exhausted there is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: ' But if one employs them unjustly and levies taxes as though never satisfied, when wealth is exhausted resentment follows, and when strength is exhausted rebellion follows.

sentences.zh: 昔禹制九等而康歌興，周人十一而頌聲作。

translations.literal: Formerly Yu established nine grades and songs of contentment arose; the Zhou people took one in eleven and hymns of praise were composed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yu established the nine grades of land, and songs of contentment arose; the Zhou took one part in eleven, and hymns of praise were composed.

sentences.zh: 於是東周遷洛，諸侯不軌，魯宣初稅畝，鄭產為丘賦，先王之制，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Zhou moved to Luoyang, the feudal lords fell out of line, Duke Xuan of Lu first taxed by the mu, Zichan of Zheng made the hill levy, and of the former kings' institutions not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Eastern Zhou moved to Luoyang, the feudal lords fell into disorder, Duke Xuan of Lu first taxed fields by the mu, and Zichan of Zheng instituted the hill levy—of the ancient kings' institutions scarcely a trace survived.

sentences.zh: 秦氏起自西戎，力正天下，驅之以刑罰，棄之以仁恩，以太半之收，長城絕於地脉，以頭會之斂，屯戍窮於嶺外。

translations.literal: The Qin clan arose from the western Rong, by force corrected the realm, drove the people with punishments and abandoned them with benevolence and grace, with collections of more than half, the Long Wall severed the earth's veins, with levies to the last head, garrison duty exhausted men beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin rose from the western borderlands and by force brought the realm to order; they drove the people with punishments and cast aside benevolence, taking more than half the harvest, building the Great Wall across the land's veins, and levying taxes to the last coin while garrison labor exhausted men beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖承秦凋敝，十五稅一，中元繼武，府廪彌殷。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han inherited Qin's exhaustion; one part in fifteen was taxed; in the Zhongyuan era martial glory continued and the granaries grew ever fuller.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han inherited Qin's exhaustion and taxed at one part in fifteen; under the Zhongyuan reign martial glory continued and the state granaries grew ever fuller.

sentences.zh: 世宗得之，用成雄侈，開邊擊胡，蕭然咸罄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu obtained it and used it to achieve grandeur and extravagance, opened the frontiers and struck the Hu, and all was suddenly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu inherited this prosperity and turned it to grandeur and extravagance; he opened the frontiers to strike the Xiongnu until the treasury was utterly drained.

sentences.zh: 宮宇捫於天漢，巡遊跨於海表，旱歲除道，凶年嘗秣，戶口以之減半，盜賊以之公行。

translations.literal: Palaces reached to the Milky Way, tours and hunts crossed beyond the seas; in drought years roads were cleared, in famine years fodder was tasted; the registered population was thereby halved, and banditry walked openly.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces reached toward the Milky Way, imperial tours crossed the seas; in drought years roads were cleared for the emperor, in famine years fodder was procured for his horses—the registered population was halved, and banditry flourished openly.

sentences.zh: 於是譎詭賦稅，異端俱起，賦及童齓，算至船車。

translations.literal: Thereupon devious and irregular taxes and levies, every sort of anomaly arose together; levies reached infants in swaddling clothes, and the poll tax extended to boats and carts.
translations.idiomatic: Then devious taxes and irregular levies multiplied; tribute was exacted even from infants in swaddling clothes, and the poll tax reached boats and carts.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，聿遵前事，成賦單薄，足稱經遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, reverently followed the former affairs, completed levies that were thin and light, sufficient to be called far-reaching in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, reverently followed precedent, kept levies light and thin, and earned a reputation for enduring principle.

sentences.zh: 靈帝開鴻都之牓，通賣官之路，公卿州郡，各有等差。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling opened the Hongdu placard and opened the path of selling offices; dukes, ministers, provinces, and commanderies each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling posted the Hongdu placard and opened the way to selling offices; ranks for dukes, ministers, provinces, and commanderies each had their price.

sentences.zh: 漢之常科，土貢方物，帝又遣先輸中署，名為導行，天下賄成，人受其敝。

translations.literal: Han's regular categories included local tribute and regional products; the emperor also sent them first to the inner palace, called 'guiding the procession,' until bribery pervaded the realm and the people suffered the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Han's regular tribute included local products and regional goods; the emperor also required them sent first to the inner palace under the name of 'guiding the procession,' until bribery pervaded the realm and the people bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉二十一帝，宋、齊十有五主，雖用度有眾寡，租賦有重輕，大抵不能傾人產業，道關政亂。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin's twenty-one emperors and Song and Qi's fifteen rulers, though expenditures had greater and lesser amounts and rent and levies had heavier and lighter rates, for the most part they could not overturn people's livelihoods or bring governance to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei's and Jin's twenty-one emperors through Song's and Qi's fifteen rulers, though expenditures varied in scale and rent and levies in weight, for the most part they did not ruin people's livelihoods or bring governance to ruin.

translations.literal: [Note: '政' should read '治'; altered under Tang taboo.]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: the character for 'governance' should read 'order and disorder'; altered under Tang dynastic taboo.]

sentences.zh: 隋文帝既平江表，天下大同，躬先儉約，以事府帑。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen of Sui pacified the lands south of the Yangtze, the realm was greatly unified; he personally took the lead in frugality to serve the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui pacified the lands south of the Yangtze and unified the realm, he personally led the way in frugality to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 開皇十七年，戶口滋盛，中外倉庫，無不盈積。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaihuang, the registered population flourished; inner and outer granaries and storehouses were all overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 17 the registered population surged; granaries and storehouses throughout the empire overflowed with grain.

sentences.zh: 所有賚給，不踰經費，京司帑屋既充，積於廊廡之下，高祖遂停此年正賦，以賜黎元。

translations.literal: All grants and gifts did not exceed regular expenditures; when the capital offices' treasury rooms were full and grain piled beneath the corridors, Gaozu stopped the regular levy of that year and bestowed it upon the common people.
translations.idiomatic: All grants and gifts stayed within regular expenditure; when the capital treasuries were full and grain piled beneath the corridors, Gaozu suspended that year's regular levy and bestowed it upon the people.

sentences.zh: 煬皇嗣守鴻基，國家殷富，雅愛宏玩，肆情方騁，初造東都，窮諸巨麗。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded to the great foundation; the state was rich and abundant; he elegantly loved grand curiosities, indulged his feelings and was just spreading his wings; he first built the Eastern Capital and exhausted every magnificence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang inherited the great foundation when the state was rich and abundant; he loved grand curiosities and indulged his desires without restraint; he first built the Eastern Capital and pursued every extravagance.

sentences.zh: 帝昔居藩翰，親平江左，兼以梁、陳曲折，以就規摹。

translations.literal: The emperor formerly resided as a prince on the frontier, personally pacified the lands east of the Yangtze, and also took Liang and Chen's twists and turns to complete his design.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince on the frontier, the emperor had personally pacified the lands east of the Yangtze, and he also drew on Liang and Chen's architectural styles to shape his design.

sentences.zh: 曾雉踰芒，浮橋跨洛，金門象闕，咸竦飛觀，頹巖塞川，構成雲綺，移嶺樹以為林藪，包芒山以為苑囿。

translations.literal: Battlements exceeded Mang Hill, floating bridges crossed the Luo, the Golden Gate and Elephant Watchtower all rose in flying towers; crumbling cliffs blocked rivers and formed cloud brocade; ridge trees were moved to make groves, and Mang Hill was enclosed as a park.
translations.idiomatic: Battlements rose higher than Mang Hill, floating bridges spanned the Luo River, the Golden Gate and Elephant Watchtower soared in flying towers; crumbling cliffs dammed rivers into brocade clouds; trees from the ridges were transplanted to form groves, and Mang Hill was enclosed as an imperial park.

sentences.zh: 長城御河，不計於人力，運驢武馬，指期於百姓，天下死於役而家傷於財。

translations.literal: The Long Wall and Imperial Canal did not count human labor; transporting mules and war horses was fixed on a schedule for the common people; the realm died in corvée and families were wounded in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Wall and Imperial Canal paid no heed to human cost; transport of mules and war horses was scheduled at the people's expense—the realm perished in corvée labor and households were ruined in wealth.

sentences.zh: 既而一討渾庭，三駕遼澤，天子親伐，師兵大舉，飛糧輓秣，水陸交至。

translations.literal: Then one campaign against the Hun court, three imperial visits to Liaozhe; the Son of Heaven personally attacked, armies were greatly raised, flying grain and fodder were transported, and land and water supplies arrived together.
translations.idiomatic: Then came one campaign against the Tujue court and three imperial tours to Liaozhe; the emperor personally took the field, armies were raised on a vast scale, grain and fodder were rushed by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 疆埸之所傾敗，勞敝之所殂殞，雖復太半不歸，而每年興發，比屋良家之子，多赴於邊陲，分離哭泣之聲，連響於州縣。

translations.literal: Where the frontier collapsed, where exhaustion and toil caused death—even though more than half did not return, every year levies were raised; from every good household sons mostly went to the border; sounds of parting and weeping echoed through the provinces and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Where the frontier collapsed and exhaustion claimed lives—even though more than half never returned, levies were raised every year; sons from every respectable household were sent to the borders, and cries of parting echoed through province after county.

sentences.zh: 老弱耕稼，不足以救飢餒，婦工紡績，不足以贍資裝。

translations.literal: The old and weak tilled but could not save them from hunger; women spun and wove but could not supply travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The old and weak tilled the fields but could not stave off hunger; women spun and wove but could not supply travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 九區之內，鸞和歲動，從行宮掖，常十萬人，所有供須，皆仰州縣。

translations.literal: Within the nine regions the imperial carriage moved every year; the palace women who accompanied him regularly numbered a hundred thousand; all supplies needed were borne by the provinces and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Within the nine regions the imperial carriage moved every year; the palace women in attendance regularly numbered a hundred thousand, and all supplies depended on the provinces and counties.

sentences.zh: 租賦之外，一切徵斂，趣以周備，不顧元元，吏因割剝，盜其太半。

translations.literal: Beyond rent and levies, everything was requisitioned and collected, hastening to completeness, heedless of the common people; officials thereby extorted and seized more than half for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond rent and regular levies, every sort of exaction was imposed to make supplies complete, with no regard for the people; officials extorted and kept more than half for themselves.

sentences.zh: 遐方珍膳，必登庖厨，翔禽毛羽，用為玩飾，買以供官，千倍其價。

translations.literal: Rare delicacies from distant regions necessarily entered the kitchens; flying birds' feathers were used as ornaments; buying to supply the court cost a thousand times the price.
translations.idiomatic: Rare delicacies from distant lands always reached the imperial kitchens; the feathers of wild birds served as ornaments; purchases for the court cost a thousandfold the ordinary price.

sentences.zh: 人愁不堪，離棄室宇，長吏叩扉而達曙，猛犬迎吠而終夕。

translations.literal: People, unable to bear their grief, abandoned their dwellings; district officials knocked on doors until dawn, and fierce dogs barked in greeting all night.
translations.idiomatic: People, crushed by their burdens, abandoned their homes; district officials knocked on doors until dawn, and fierce dogs barked at visitors through the night.

sentences.zh: 自燕、趙跨於齊、韓，江、淮入於襄、鄧，東周洛邑之地，西秦隴山之右，僭偽交侵，盜賊充斥。

translations.literal: From Yan and Zhao across Qi and Han, from the Jiang and Huai into Xiang and Deng, the lands of Eastern Zhou's Luoyang and western Qin's lands beyond Longshan—usurpers and rebels invaded each other, and bandits filled the land.
translations.idiomatic: From Yan and Zhao across Qi and Han, from the Jiang and Huai into Xiang and Deng, from the lands of Eastern Zhou's Luoyang to western Qin beyond Longshan—usurpers and rebels clashed, and bandits filled the land.

sentences.zh: 宮觀鞠為茂草，鄉亭絕其煙火，人相啖食，十而四五。

translations.literal: Palaces and temples became rank grass; village posts lost their cooking smoke; people ate one another—four or five in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces and temples turned to rank weeds; village posts lost their cooking smoke; people ate one another—four or five in ten.

sentences.zh: 關中癘疫，炎旱傷稼，代王開永豐之粟，以振飢人，去倉數百里，老幼雲集。

translations.literal: Plague struck Guanzhong, scorching drought harmed the crops; Prince Dai opened the grain of Yongfeng to relieve the hungry; hundreds of li from the granary, old and young gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Plague struck Guanzhong and scorching drought ruined the harvest; Prince Dai opened the Yongfeng granary to feed the hungry; old and young gathered like clouds hundreds of li from the granary.

sentences.zh: 吏在貪殘，官無攸次，咸資鏹貨，動移旬月，頓臥墟野，欲返不能，死人如積，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Officials were greedy and cruel, offices had no order; all demanded bribes; movement took ten-day periods and more; they collapsed in the wilderness, wishing to return but unable; the dead piled like heaps, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were greedy and cruel, government had no order; all demanded bribes; journeys took months; people collapsed in the wilderness, unable to return; the dead piled in heaps beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 雖復皇王撫運，天祿有終，而隋氏之亡，亦由於此。

translations.literal: Although the sage kings received Heaven's mandate and heavenly fortune has its end, the fall of the Sui house also came from this.
translations.idiomatic: Though sage kings receive Heaven's mandate and heavenly fortune must end, the fall of the Sui dynasty also came from this.

sentences.zh: 馬遷為平準書，班固述食貨志，上下數千載，損益粗舉。

translations.literal: Ma Qian wrote the Treatise on the Equalization of Goods; Ban Gu narrated the Treatise on Food and Money; spanning several thousand years above and below, gains and losses are roughly set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian wrote the Treatise on the Equalization of Goods and Ban Gu the Treatise on Food and Money; spanning several thousand years, they roughly set forth what was gained and lost.

sentences.zh: 自此史官曾無概見。

translations.literal: From this time the historiographers never had a general survey.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the official historians never produced a comprehensive survey.

sentences.zh: 夫厥初生人，食貨為本。

translations.literal: When people first arose, food and goods were the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When people first arose, food and goods were the foundation of life.

sentences.zh: 聖王割廬井以業之，通貨財以富之。

translations.literal: The sage kings divided huts and wells to give them occupations, circulated goods and wealth to enrich them.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings divided land into huts and wells to give the people their occupations and circulated goods and wealth to enrich them.

sentences.zh: 富而教之，仁義以之興，貧而為盜，刑罰不能止。

translations.literal: When enriched, teach them; benevolence and righteousness thereby arise; when poor they become bandits, and punishments cannot stop them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are enriched, teach them—benevolence and righteousness then flourish; when they are poor they turn to banditry, and punishments cannot stop them.

sentences.zh: 故為食貨志，用編前書之末云。

translations.literal: Therefore this Treatise on Food and Money is compiled at the end of the preceding books.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore this Treatise on Food and Money is compiled to conclude the preceding books.

sentences.zh: 晉自中原喪亂，元帝寓居江左，百姓之自拔南奔者，並謂之僑人。

translations.literal: After Jin lost the Central Plains to chaos, Emperor Yuan resided east of the Yangtze; common people who escaped south on their own were all called émigrés.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin lost the Central Plains to chaos, Emperor Yuan established his court east of the Yangtze; common people who fled south on their own were all called émigrés.

sentences.zh: 皆取舊壤之名，僑立郡縣，往往散居，無有土著。

translations.literal: All took names of old territories and established émigré commanderies and counties; they often lived scattered, with no fixed native places.
translations.idiomatic: They took names from their old homelands and established émigré commanderies and counties; they often lived scattered, with no fixed native registration.

sentences.zh: 而江南之俗，火耕水耨，土地卑濕，無有蓄積之資。

translations.literal: But the customs of Jiangnan were slash-and-burn and water-rice cultivation; the land was low and damp, with no resources for accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: But Jiangnan custom was slash-and-burn and water-rice cultivation; the land was low and damp, with little capacity for accumulation.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻陬俚洞，霑沐王化者，各隨輕重，收其賧物，以裨國用。

translations.literal: Among the various Man tribes, Li caves, and Dong settlements touched by royal transformation, each according to lighter or heavier status collected their tribute goods to supplement state use.
translations.idiomatic: Among the various Man tribes, Li settlements, and Dong communities touched by royal civilization, tribute was collected according to rank to supplement state revenue.

sentences.zh: 又嶺外酋帥，因生口翡翠明珠犀象之饒，雄於鄉曲者，朝廷多因而署之，以收其利。

translations.literal: Also chieftains beyond the mountain passes, because of the abundance of captives, jadeite, pearls, rhinoceros horn, and elephants, who were powerful in their districts—the court often appointed them accordingly to collect their profit.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains beyond the passes, enriched by captives, jadeite, pearls, rhinoceros horn, and elephants and powerful in their districts, were often appointed by the court to collect tribute for the state.

sentences.zh: 歷宋、齊、梁、陳，皆因而不改。

translations.literal: Through Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen, all followed this without change.
translations.idiomatic: Through Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen, this practice continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其軍國所須雜物，隨土所出，臨時折課市取，乃無恒法定令。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous goods needed for military and state use, according to what each region produced, were temporarily assessed and purchased in the market—there were no fixed laws or orders.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous goods needed for military and state use were purchased locally according to regional products through temporary assessments—there were no fixed statutes.

sentences.zh: 列州郡縣，制其任土所出，以為徵賦。

translations.literal: Provinces, commanderies, and counties were listed, fixing what each region's soil produced as the basis for levies and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces, commanderies, and counties were assigned fixed products of their soil as the basis for levies and tribute.

sentences.zh: 其無貫之人，不樂州縣編戶者，謂之浮浪人，樂輸亦無定數，任量，准所輸，[2]終優於正課焉。

translations.literal: Those without registration who did not wish to be registered in provincial and county household rolls were called floating drifters; voluntary contributions also had no fixed amount, according to quantity, based on what was contributed, [Note: Tongdian reads '惟' for '准'] ultimately still better than the regular levy.
translations.idiomatic: Those without registration who refused provincial and county household rolls were called floating drifters; their voluntary contributions had no fixed amount but were assessed by quantity—[Note: the Tongdian reads 'only' for 'according to']—yet still ultimately lighter than the regular levy.

sentences.zh: 都下人多為諸王公貴人左右、佃客、典計、衣食客之類，皆無課役。

translations.literal: Many in the capital served princes, dukes, and nobles as attendants, tenant clients, stewards, and clothing-and-food clients—all exempt from levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the capital served princes, dukes, and nobles as attendants, tenant clients, stewards, and provision clients—all exempt from levies and corvée.

sentences.zh: 官品第一第二，佃客無過四十戶。

translations.literal: For official ranks first and second, tenant clients could not exceed forty households.
translations.idiomatic: For ranks one and two, tenant clients could not exceed forty households.

sentences.zh: 第三品三十五戶。

translations.literal: Third rank: thirty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: thirty-five households.

sentences.zh: 第四品三十戶。

translations.literal: Fourth rank: thirty households.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: thirty households.

sentences.zh: 第五品二十五戶。

translations.literal: Fifth rank: twenty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: twenty-five households.

sentences.zh: 第六品二十戶。

translations.literal: Sixth rank: twenty households.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: twenty households.

sentences.zh: 第七品十五戶。

translations.literal: Seventh rank: fifteen households.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank: fifteen households.

sentences.zh: 第八品十戶。

translations.literal: Eighth rank: ten households.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank: ten households.

sentences.zh: 第九品五戶。

translations.literal: Ninth rank: five households.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank: five households.

sentences.zh: 其佃穀，皆與大家量分。

translations.literal: Their tenant grain was all divided by measure with the great families.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from tenant fields was divided by measure with the great families.

sentences.zh: 其典計，官品第一第二，置三人。

translations.literal: For stewards, ranks first and second were allotted three persons.
translations.idiomatic: For stewards, ranks one and two were allotted three persons.

sentences.zh: 第三第四，置二人。

translations.literal: Third and fourth, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks, two persons.

sentences.zh: 第五第六及公府參軍、殿中監、監軍、長史、司馬、部曲督、關外侯、材官、議郎已上，一人。

translations.literal: Fifth and sixth, and ducal-house staff officers, palace supervisors, army supervisors, chief administrators, marshals, commanders of private troops, marquises outside the passes, materiel officers, and advisory gentlemen and above—one person.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth and sixth ranks, and ducal-house staff officers, palace supervisors, army supervisors, chief administrators, marshals, commanders of private troops, marquises outside the passes, materiel officers, and advisory gentlemen and above—one person each.

sentences.zh: 皆通在佃客數中。

translations.literal: All were counted within the tenant-client quota.
translations.idiomatic: All were counted within the tenant-client quota.

sentences.zh: 官品第六已上，并得衣食客三人。

translations.literal: From official rank sixth and above, each also received three clothing-and-food clients.
translations.idiomatic: From rank six and above, each also received three provision clients.

sentences.zh: 第七第八二人。

translations.literal: Seventh and eighth, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh and eighth ranks, two persons.

sentences.zh: 第九品及轝輦、跡禽、前驅、由基強弩司馬、羽林郎、殿中冗從武賁、殿中武賁、持椎斧武騎武賁、持鈒冗從武賁、命中武賁武騎，一人。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and imperial carriage attendants, trace-hunters, vanguard runners, Youji strong-crossbow marshals, Forest Guard gentlemen, palace supernumerary warrior guards, palace warrior guards, mace-and-axe cavalry warrior guards, supernumerary warrior guards with iron clubs, and marksmanship cavalry warrior guards—one person.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank and imperial carriage attendants, trace-hunters, vanguard runners, Youji strong-crossbow marshals, Forest Guard gentlemen, palace supernumerary warrior guards, palace warrior guards, mace-and-axe cavalry warrior guards, supernumerary warrior guards with iron clubs, and marksmanship cavalry warrior guards—one person each.

sentences.zh: 客皆注家籍。

translations.literal: Clients were all registered on the household rolls of their masters.
translations.idiomatic: All clients were registered on their masters' household rolls.

sentences.zh: 其課，丁男調布絹各二丈，絲三兩，綿八兩，祿絹八尺，祿綿三兩二分，租米五石，祿米二石。

translations.literal: The levy: adult males paid two zhang each of cloth and silk, three liang of silk thread, eight liang of cotton, eight chi of salary silk, three liang two fen of salary cotton, five shi of rent grain, and two shi of salary grain.
translations.idiomatic: The levy on adult males: two zhang each of cloth and silk, three liang of silk thread, eight liang of cotton, eight chi of salary silk, three liang two fen of salary cotton, five shi of rent grain, and two shi of salary grain.

sentences.zh: 丁女並半之。

translations.literal: Adult females paid half.
translations.idiomatic: Adult females paid half.

sentences.zh: 男女年十六已上至六十，為丁。

translations.literal: Males and females from sixteen up to sixty were counted as adult laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Males and females from age sixteen to sixty were counted as adult laborers.

sentences.zh: 男年十六，亦半課，年十八正課，六十六免課。

translations.literal: Males at sixteen also paid half the levy; at eighteen the full levy; at sixty-six exempt from the levy.
translations.idiomatic: Males at sixteen paid half the levy; at eighteen the full levy; at sixty-six they were exempt.

sentences.zh: 女以嫁者為丁，若在室者，年二十乃為丁。

translations.literal: Females counted as adult laborers when married; if unmarried, only at twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Married women counted as adult laborers; unmarried women only at age twenty.

sentences.zh: 其男丁，每歲役不過二十日。

translations.literal: For adult males, corvée each year did not exceed twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Adult males owed no more than twenty days of corvée per year.

sentences.zh: 又率十八人出一運丁役之。

translations.literal: Also, one transport corvée laborer was levied from every eighteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Also, one transport corvée laborer was levied from every eighteen persons.

sentences.zh: 其田，畝稅米二斗。

translations.literal: For fields, the tax was two dou of grain per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were taxed two dou of grain per mu.

sentences.zh: 蓋大率如此。

translations.literal: Generally the overall rate was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Generally the overall rate was as described.

sentences.zh: 其度量，斗則三斗當今一斗，稱則三兩當今一兩，尺則一尺二寸當今一尺。

translations.literal: For measures: three dou equaled one present-day dou; three liang equaled one present-day liang; one chi two cun equaled one present-day chi.
translations.idiomatic: For measures: three dou equaled one present-day dou; three liang equaled one present-day liang; one chi two cun equaled one present-day chi.

sentences.zh: 其倉，京都有龍首倉，即石頭津倉也，臺城內倉，南塘倉，常平倉，東、西太倉，東宮倉，所貯總不過五十餘萬。

translations.literal: For granaries: in the capital there were Longshou Granary—that is, Shitoujin Granary—Inner City Granary, Nantang Granary, Ever-Normal Granary, East and West Great Granaries, and Eastern Palace Granary; total stored grain did not exceed five hundred thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital there were Longshou Granary (that is, Shitoujin Granary), Inner City Granary, Nantang Granary, Ever-Normal Granary, East and West Great Granaries, and Eastern Palace Granary; total storage did not exceed five hundred thousand-plus.

sentences.zh: 在外有豫章倉、釣磯倉、錢塘倉，並是大貯備之處。

translations.literal: Outside there were Yuzhang Granary, Diaoji Granary, and Qiantang Granary—all major reserve storage places.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital were Yuzhang Granary, Diaoji Granary, and Qiantang Granary—all major reserve depots.

sentences.zh: 自餘諸州郡臺傳，亦各有倉。

translations.literal: The remaining provinces, commanderies, and relay stations each also had granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Other provinces, commanderies, and relay stations each also had granaries.

sentences.zh: 大抵自侯景之亂，國用常褊。

translations.literal: Generally from the chaos of Hou Jing onward, state revenue was constantly strained.
translations.idiomatic: Generally from Hou Jing's rebellion onward, state revenue was constantly strained.

sentences.zh: 京官文武，月別唯得廪食，多遙帶一郡縣官而取其祿秩焉。

translations.literal: Capital civil and military officials monthly received only grain rations; many remotely held a commandery or county office and took its salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Capital civil and military officials received only monthly grain rations; many remotely held a commandery or county post and drew its salary and rank.

sentences.zh: 揚、徐等大州，比令、僕班。

translations.literal: Large provinces like Yang and Xu ranked with ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Large provinces like Yang and Xu ranked with ministers.

sentences.zh: 寧、桂等小州，比參軍班。

translations.literal: Small provinces like Ning and Gui ranked with staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Small provinces like Ning and Gui ranked with staff officers.

sentences.zh: 丹陽、吳郡、會稽等郡，同太子詹事、尚書班。

translations.literal: Commanderies like Danyang, Wu, and Kuaiji ranked with the Crown Prince's household superintendent and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies like Danyang, Wu, and Kuaiji ranked with the Crown Prince's household superintendent and ministers.

sentences.zh: 高涼、晉康等小郡，三班而已。

translations.literal: Small commanderies like Gaoliang and Jinkang, only three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Small commanderies like Gaoliang and Jinkang ranked only three grades.

sentences.zh: 大縣六班，小縣兩轉方至一班。

translations.literal: Large counties six grades; small counties required two promotions to reach one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Large counties ranked six grades; small counties required two promotions to reach one grade.

sentences.zh: 品第既殊，不可委載。

translations.literal: Since the grades differed, they cannot all be listed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Since the grades differed, they cannot all be listed in detail.

sentences.zh: [3]州郡縣祿米絹布絲綿，當處輸臺傳倉庫。

translations.literal: [Note: '妄' in the preceding sentence should read '委' (detail); corrected per Tongdian 35.] Province, commandery, and county salary grain, silk, cloth, thread, and cotton were delivered locally to relay granaries and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: [Note: 'cannot all be wrongly listed' in the preceding sentence should read 'cannot all be listed in detail; corrected per the Tongdian.] Province, commandery, and county salary grain, silk, cloth, thread, and cotton were delivered locally to relay granaries and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 若給刺史守令等，先准其所部文武人物多少，由敕而裁。

translations.literal: When supplying prefects, magistrates, and the like, first according to the number of civil and military personnel in their jurisdiction, it was decided by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: When supplying prefects, magistrates, and the like, allocations were first determined by the number of civil and military personnel in their jurisdiction, as decided by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 凡如此祿秩，既通所部兵士給之，其家所得蓋少。

translations.literal: Generally such salaries, since they also supplied the garrison soldiers of the jurisdiction, what the household actually received was very little.
translations.idiomatic: Since such salaries also had to supply garrison soldiers in the jurisdiction, what the official's household actually received was very little.

sentences.zh: 諸王諸主，出閤就第婚冠所須，及衣裳服飾，并酒米魚鮭香油紙燭等，並官給之。

translations.literal: Princes and princesses, when leaving the palace for their estates for marriage and capping ceremonies, and clothing and adornments, as well as wine, grain, fish, salmon, fragrant oil, paper, candles, and the like, were all supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and princesses, when leaving the palace for their estates for marriage and capping ceremonies, and for clothing, adornments, wine, grain, fish, salmon, fragrant oil, paper, candles, and the like, were all supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 王及主婿外祿者，不給。

translations.literal: Princes and princesses' husbands who held external salaries were not supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and princesses' husbands who held external salaries received no such provision.

sentences.zh: 解任還京，仍亦公給云。

translations.literal: When relieved of office and returning to the capital, they were still publicly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When relieved of office and returning to the capital, they were still publicly supplied.

sentences.zh: 魏自永安之後，政道陵夷，寇亂實繁，農商失業。

translations.literal: After Yong'an in Wei, governance declined, banditry and chaos were truly numerous, and farmers and merchants lost their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's Yong'an era, governance declined, banditry and chaos multiplied, and farmers and merchants lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 官有征伐，皆權調於人，猶不足以相資奉，乃令所在迭相糾發，百姓愁怨，無復聊生。

translations.literal: When the government had campaigns, all were temporarily levied from the people; still insufficient to support each other, then ordered each locality to take turns requisitioning; the people groaned in resentment and had no life left.
translations.idiomatic: When the state launched campaigns, levies were imposed on the people; even these were insufficient for support, so localities were ordered to requisition in rotation—the people groaned in resentment and could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 尋而六鎮擾亂，相率內徙，寓食於齊、晉之郊。

translations.literal: Soon the Six Garrisons were disturbed and in chaos; they led one another in migrating inward and lived as guests eating in the Qi and Jin borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Six Garrisons fell into turmoil; garrison soldiers migrated inward in waves and lived as dependents in the Qi and Jin borderlands.

sentences.zh: 齊神武因之，以成大業。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu took advantage of this to achieve his great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan of Northern Qi seized on this to build his great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 魏武西遷，連年戰爭，河、洛之間，又並空竭。

translations.literal: When Wei Wu moved west, war continued year after year; between the Yellow and Luo rivers all was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, war continued year after year; the lands between the Yellow and Luo rivers were utterly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 天平元年，遷都於鄴，出粟一百三十萬石，以振貧人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping, the capital moved to Ye; one million three hundred thousand shi of grain was issued to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year 1 the capital moved to Ye; 1.3 million shi of grain was issued to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 是時六坊之眾，從武帝而西者，不能萬人，餘皆北徙，並給常廪，春秋二時賜帛，以供衣服之費。

translations.literal: At that time of the masses of the Six Camps who followed Emperor Wu west, not ten thousand could go; the rest all moved north and were given regular rations; in spring and autumn silk was bestowed for clothing expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Six Camps masses who followed Emperor Wu west, fewer than ten thousand could go; the rest moved north and received regular rations, with silk bestowed in spring and autumn for clothing.

sentences.zh: 常調之外，逐豐稔之處，折絹糴粟，以充國儲。

translations.literal: Beyond the regular levy, in places of abundant harvest, silk was assessed and grain purchased to fill the state stores.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the regular levy, in regions of abundant harvest silk was assessed and grain purchased to fill the state stores.

sentences.zh: 於諸州緣河津濟，皆官倉貯積，以擬漕運。

translations.literal: Along the river crossings at the borders of the various provinces, official granaries were set up to store grain for canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: At river crossings along provincial borders, official granaries were established to store grain for canal transport.

sentences.zh: 於滄、瀛、幽、青四州之境，傍海置鹽官，以煮鹽，每歲收錢，軍國之資，得以周贍。

translations.literal: In the territory of Cang, Ying, You, and Qing four provinces along the sea, salt offices were placed to boil salt; each year money was collected, and military and state funds were thereby sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In Cang, Ying, You, and Qing along the coast, salt offices were established to boil salt; revenue collected each year fully supplied military and state expenses.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，倉廪充實，雖有水旱凶饑之處，皆仰開倉以振之。

translations.literal: From this time granaries were full; though there were places of flood, drought, and famine, all relied on opening granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: From this time granaries were full; even where flood, drought, and famine struck, relief came from opening the granaries.

sentences.zh: 元象、興和之中，頻歲大穰。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang and Xinghe periods, year after year brought great harvests.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang and Xinghe periods harvests were abundant year after year.

sentences.zh: 穀斛至九錢。

translations.literal: Grain per hu reached nine cash.
translations.idiomatic: Grain sold for as little as nine cash per hu.

sentences.zh: 是時法網寬弛，百姓多離舊居，闕於徭賦。

translations.literal: At that time the legal net was loose; many common people left their old residences and were absent from corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the legal net was loose; many common people left their old homes and evaded corvée and levies.

sentences.zh: 神武乃命孫騰、高隆之，分括無籍之戶，得六十餘萬。

translations.literal: Shenwu then ordered Sun Teng and Gao Longzhi to investigate households without registration and obtained more than six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then ordered Sun Teng and Gao Longzhi to investigate unregistered households and found more than six hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 於是僑居者各勒還本屬，是後租調之入有加焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon émigrés were each compelled to return to their original jurisdictions; afterward revenue from rent and levies increased.
translations.idiomatic: Émigrés were then compelled to return to their original jurisdictions, and rent and levy revenue increased.

sentences.zh: 及文襄嗣業，侯景背叛，河南之地，困於兵革。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded, Hou Jing rebelled; the lands of Henan were distressed by war.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded, Hou Jing rebelled and the Henan region was ravaged by war.

sentences.zh: 尋而侯景亂梁，乃命行臺辛術，略有淮南之地。

translations.literal: Soon Hou Jing disturbed Liang; then the mobile headquarters Xin Shu was ordered to seize somewhat the lands of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Jing threw Liang into chaos; the mobile headquarters under Xin Shu was ordered to seize parts of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 其新附州郡，覊縻輕稅而已。

translations.literal: The newly attached provinces and commanderies were only loosely controlled with light taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Newly attached provinces and commanderies were only loosely controlled with light taxes.

sentences.zh: 及文宣受禪，多所創革。

translations.literal: When Wuxuan received the abdication, many things were newly created and reformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan received the abdication, many institutions were newly created and reformed.

sentences.zh: 六坊之內徙者，更加簡練，每一人必當百人，任其臨陣必死，然後取之，謂之百保鮮卑。

translations.literal: Those of the Six Camps who migrated inward were further selected and refined; each man had to equal a hundred men, only after being able to face battle and surely die were they taken—called the Hundred-Strong Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the Six Camps who migrated inward were further selected and trained; each man had to equal a hundred ordinary soldiers and was taken only if willing to die in battle—they were called the Hundred-Strong Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 又簡華人之勇力絕倫者，謂之勇士，以備邊要。

translations.literal: Also selected among Han people those of unmatched courage and strength, called warriors, to guard the frontier posts.
translations.idiomatic: Han men of unmatched courage were also selected as warriors to guard the frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 始立九等之戶，富者稅其錢，貧者役其力。

translations.literal: First the nine-grade household system was established: the rich paid in money, the poor in labor.
translations.idiomatic: The nine-grade household system was first established: the rich paid in money, the poor in labor.

sentences.zh: 北興長城之役，南有金陵之戰。

translations.literal: In the north the Long Wall corvée was raised; in the south there was the Jinling campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the north the Great Wall corvée was raised; in the south there was the Jinling campaign.

sentences.zh: 其後南征諸將，頻歲陷沒，士馬死者，以數十萬計。

translations.literal: Afterward southern expedition generals year after year were defeated; soldiers and horses who died numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward southern expedition generals were defeated year after year; soldiers and horses lost numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 重以修創臺殿，所役甚廣。

translations.literal: Added to this was the repair and construction of terraces and halls; corvée labor employed was very extensive.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this was the repair and construction of terraces and halls; corvée labor was very extensive.

sentences.zh: 而帝刑罰酷濫，吏道因而成姦，豪黨兼并，戶口益多隱漏。

translations.literal: But the emperor's punishments were cruel and excessive; official ways thereby became corrupt; powerful cliques merged holdings and household registration increasingly had hidden omissions.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor's punishments were cruel and excessive; officials grew corrupt; powerful cliques merged holdings and household registration had ever more hidden omissions.

sentences.zh: 舊制，未娶者輸半牀租調，陽翟一郡，戶至數萬，籍多無妻。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the unmarried paid half a bed's rent and levy; Yangdi one commandery had households reaching tens of thousands, registers mostly without wives.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system the unmarried paid half a bed's rent and levy; in Yangdi Commandery alone households reached tens of thousands, yet registers mostly listed no wives.

sentences.zh: 有司劾之，帝以為生事。

translations.literal: The responsible officials impeached this; the emperor considered it making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Responsible officials impeached this; the emperor considered it meddling.

sentences.zh: 由是姦欺尤甚。

translations.literal: From this fraud and deception was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: From this fraud and deception grew especially severe.

sentences.zh: 戶口租調，十亡六七。

translations.literal: Household registration rent and levies—six or seven in ten were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Of household registration rent and levies, six or seven tenths were lost.

sentences.zh: 是時用度轉廣，賜與無節，府藏之積，不足以供，乃減百官之祿，撤軍人常廪，併省州郡縣鎮戍之職。

translations.literal: At that time expenditures turned increasingly broad; grants and gifts had no limit; treasury stores were insufficient to supply; then officials' salaries were reduced, soldiers' regular rations cut, and provincial, commandery, county, and garrison posts merged and eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditures grew ever broader and grants had no limit; treasury stores could not supply them; officials' salaries were reduced, soldiers' regular rations cut, and provincial, commandery, county, and garrison posts merged or eliminated.

sentences.zh: 又制刺史守宰行兼者，並不給幹，以節國之費用焉。

translations.literal: Also instituted that prefects and magistrates who concurrently held posts received no clerks, to economize state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: It was also instituted that prefects and magistrates holding concurrent posts received no clerks, to economize state expenses.

sentences.zh: 天保八年，議徙冀、定、瀛無田之人，謂之樂遷，於幽州范陽寬鄉以處之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, it was proposed to move people of Ji, Ding, and Ying without fields, called 'joyful migrants,' to Fangyang in Youzhou's wide districts.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 8 it was proposed to move landless people of Ji, Ding, and Ying—called 'joyful migrants'—to the wide districts of Fangyang in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 百姓驚擾。

translations.literal: The common people were alarmed and disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were alarmed and disturbed.

sentences.zh: 屬以頻歲不熟，米糴踊貴矣。

translations.literal: It happened that year after year harvests failed and grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests failed year after year and grain prices soared.

sentences.zh: 廢帝乾明中，尚書左丞蘇珍芝，議修石鼈等屯，歲收數萬石。

translations.literal: In the Qianming era of Emperor Fei, Left Assistant Director Su Zhenzhi proposed repairing the Shibie and other garrison farms, collecting tens of thousands of shi each year.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Fei's Qianming era, Left Assistant Director Su Zhenzhi proposed repairing the Shibie and other garrison farms, yielding tens of thousands of shi each year.

sentences.zh: 自是淮南軍防，糧廪充足。

translations.literal: From this the Huainan military defenses had abundant grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Huainan military defenses had abundant grain stores.

sentences.zh: 孝昭皇建中，平州刺史嵇曄建議，開幽州督亢舊陂，長城左右營屯，歲收稻粟數十萬石，北境得以周贍。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian era of Emperor Xiaozhao, Pingzhou Prefect Ji Ye proposed opening the old embankments of Youzhou's Dukang, garrison farms left and right of the Long Wall, collecting hundreds of thousands of shi of rice each year; the northern border was thereby sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaozhao's Huangjian era, Pingzhou Prefect Ji Ye proposed reopening Youzhou's old Dukang embankments and garrison farms along the Great Wall, yielding hundreds of thousands of shi of rice each year; the northern border was thereby supplied.

sentences.zh: 又於河內置懷義等屯，以給河南之費。

translations.literal: Also in Henei established Huaiyi and other garrison farms to supply Henan expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi and other garrison farms were also established in Henei to supply Henan expenses.

sentences.zh: 自是稍止轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: From this transport labor was somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: From this transport labor was somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 至河清三年定令，乃命人居十家為比鄰，五十家為閭里，百家為族黨。

translations.literal: By the third year of Heqing when the statutes were fixed, people were ordered: ten households formed a ward, fifty a neighborhood, a hundred a clan association.
translations.idiomatic: By Heqing year 3 when the statutes were fixed, people were organized: ten households formed a ward, fifty a neighborhood, a hundred a clan association.

sentences.zh: 男子十八以上，六十五已下為丁；

translations.literal: Males eighteen and above, sixty-five and below were adult laborers;
translations.idiomatic: Males eighteen and above, sixty-five and below, were adult laborers;

sentences.zh: 十六已上，十七已下為中；

translations.literal: Sixteen and above, seventeen and below were middling;
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen and above, seventeen and below, were middling;

sentences.zh: 六十六已上為老；

translations.literal: Sixty-six and above were elderly;
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-six and above were elderly;

sentences.zh: 十五已下為小。

translations.literal: Fifteen and below were minors.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen and below were minors.

sentences.zh: 率以十八受田，輸租調，二十充兵，六十免力役，六十六退田，免租調。

translations.literal: Generally at eighteen one received fields and paid rent and levies; at twenty one served as soldier; at sixty exempt from labor corvée; at sixty-six returned fields and exempt from rent and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Generally at eighteen one received fields and paid rent and levies; at twenty one entered military service; at sixty one was exempt from labor corvée; at sixty-six one returned fields and was exempt from rent and levies.

sentences.zh: 京城四面，諸坊之外三十里內為公田。

translations.literal: Within thirty li outside the four sides of the capital and outside the wards was public land.
translations.idiomatic: Within thirty li outside the capital's four sides and beyond the wards was public land.

sentences.zh: 受公田者，三縣代遷戶執事官一品已下，逮于羽林武賁，各有差。

translations.literal: Those receiving public land: within three counties, rotating households of officials from rank one and below down to Forest Guard warrior guards each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: Those receiving public land: within three counties, rotating households of officials from rank one down to Forest Guard warrior guards each had their allotted shares.

sentences.zh: 其外畿郡，華人官第一品已下，羽林武賁已上，各有差。

translations.literal: In the outer capital districts, Han officials from rank one and below, Forest Guard warrior guards and above, each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the outer capital districts, Han officials from rank one down to Forest Guard warrior guards and above each had their allotted shares.

sentences.zh: 職事及百姓請墾田者，名為永業田。

translations.literal: Functional officials and common people who requested reclaimed land were called perpetual-estate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Functional officials and common people who requested reclaimed land were granted perpetual-estate fields.

sentences.zh: [4]奴婢受田者，親王止三百人；

translations.literal: [Note: '永田' should read '永業田' (perpetual-estate fields); corrected per Cefu 495 and Tongdian 2.] For slave recipients of fields, princes of the blood were limited to three hundred persons;
translations.idiomatic: [Note: 'perpetual fields' should read 'perpetual-estate fields'; corrected per the Cefu and Tongdian.] Princes of the blood receiving fields through slaves were limited to three hundred persons;

sentences.zh: 嗣王止二百人；

translations.literal: Successor princes limited to two hundred persons;
translations.idiomatic: Successor princes were limited to two hundred persons;

sentences.zh: 第二品嗣王已下及庶姓王，止一百五十人；

translations.literal: Second-rank successor princes and below and commoner surnames' princes, limited to one hundred fifty persons;
translations.idiomatic: Second-rank successor princes and below and princes of commoner surname were limited to one hundred fifty persons;

sentences.zh: 正三品已上及皇宗，止一百人；

translations.literal: Regular third rank and above and imperial clan, limited to one hundred persons;
translations.idiomatic: Regular third rank and above and imperial clansmen were limited to one hundred persons;

sentences.zh: 七品已上，限止八十人；

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above, limited to eighty persons;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank and above were limited to eighty persons;

sentences.zh: 八品已下至庶人，限止六十人。

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below to common people, limited to sixty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank and below to commoners were limited to sixty persons.

sentences.zh: 奴婢限外不給田者，皆不輸。

translations.literal: Slaves beyond the limit who received no fields paid no levies.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves beyond the limit who received no fields paid no levies.

sentences.zh: 其方百里外及州人，一夫受露田八十畝，婦四十畝。

translations.literal: Outside a hundred li square and state people, one adult male received eighty mu of land, women forty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the hundred-li square and for state residents, one adult male received eighty mu of land, women forty mu.

sentences.zh: 奴婢依良人，限數與在京百官同。

translations.literal: Slaves followed common people; limits matched capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves followed common people; limits matched those for capital officials.

sentences.zh: 丁牛一頭，受田六十畝，限止四牛。

translations.literal: One adult ox received sixty mu of land, limited to four oxen.
translations.idiomatic: One adult ox received sixty mu of land, limited to four oxen.

sentences.zh: [5]又每丁給永業二十畝，為桑田。

translations.literal: [Note: '年' should read '牛' (oxen); corrected per Tongdian 2.] Also each adult laborer was given twenty mu of perpetual estate as mulberry fields.
translations.idiomatic: [Note: 'years' should read 'oxen'; corrected per the Tongdian.] Each adult laborer was also given twenty mu of perpetual estate as mulberry fields.

sentences.zh: 其中種桑五十根，榆三根，棗五根。

translations.literal: Among them fifty mulberry roots, three elm roots, five jujube roots were planted.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were planted fifty mulberry roots, three elm roots, and five jujube roots.

sentences.zh: 不在還受之限。

translations.literal: Not within the limit of return and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: These were not subject to return and reassignment.

sentences.zh: 非此田者，悉入還受之分。

translations.literal: Fields other than these all entered the share of return and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: All other fields entered the pool for return and reassignment.

sentences.zh: 土不宜桑者，給麻田，如桑田法。

translations.literal: Where soil was unsuitable for mulberry, hemp fields were given according to mulberry-field rules.
translations.idiomatic: Where soil was unsuitable for mulberry, hemp fields were granted under the mulberry-field rules.

sentences.zh: 率人一牀，調絹一疋，綿八兩，凡十斤綿中，折一斤作絲，墾租二石，義租五斗。

translations.literal: Generally per one bed: one bolt of silk for the levy, eight liang of cotton; of every ten jin of cotton one jin was converted to silk thread; reclaimed rent two shi, charity rent five dou.
translations.idiomatic: Generally per bed: one bolt of silk for the levy, eight liang of cotton; of every ten jin of cotton one jin was converted to silk thread; reclaimed rent two shi, charity rent five dou.

sentences.zh: 奴婢各准良人之半。

translations.literal: Male and female slaves each paid half of common people.
translations.idiomatic: Male and female slaves each paid half the common rate.

sentences.zh: 牛調二尺，墾租一斗，義租五升。

translations.literal: Ox levy two chi, reclaimed rent one dou, charity rent five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ox levy two chi, reclaimed rent one dou, charity rent five sheng.

sentences.zh: 墾租送臺，義租納郡，以備水旱。

translations.literal: Reclaimed rent was sent to the capital; charity rent was delivered to the commandery for flood and drought reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Reclaimed rent was sent to the capital; charity rent was delivered to the commandery for flood and drought reserves.

sentences.zh: 墾租皆依貧富為三梟。

translations.literal: Reclaimed rent all followed rich and poor in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Reclaimed rent was assessed in three grades according to wealth.

sentences.zh: 其賦稅常調，則少者直出上戶，中者及中戶，多者及下戶。

translations.literal: For regular levies and taxes, the few paid from upper households, the moderate from middle households, the many from lower households.
translations.idiomatic: For regular levies and taxes, the lightest burden fell on upper households, moderate on middle households, and heaviest on lower households.

sentences.zh: 上梟輸遠處，中梟輸次遠，下梟輸當州倉。

translations.literal: Upper grade delivered to distant places, middle grade to next distant, lower grade to the local provincial granary.
translations.idiomatic: The upper grade delivered to distant places, the middle to intermediate distances, the lower to the local provincial granary.

sentences.zh: 三年一校焉。

translations.literal: Every three years there was one verification.
translations.idiomatic: Verification was conducted every three years.

sentences.zh: 租入臺者，五百里內輸粟，五百里外輸米。

translations.literal: Rent entering the capital: within five hundred li delivered grain, beyond five hundred li delivered husked rice.
translations.idiomatic: Rent entering the capital: within five hundred li grain was delivered, beyond five hundred li husked rice.

sentences.zh: 入州鎮者，輸粟。

translations.literal: Entering provinces and garrisons: delivered grain.
translations.idiomatic: Entering provinces and garrisons: grain was delivered.

sentences.zh: 人欲輸錢者，准上絹收錢。

translations.literal: If people wished to pay in money, it was accepted according to upper-grade silk prices.
translations.idiomatic: Those wishing to pay in coin were charged according to upper-grade silk prices.

sentences.zh: 諸州郡皆別置富人倉。

translations.literal: All provinces and commanderies separately established rich-household granaries.
translations.idiomatic: All provinces and commanderies separately established rich-household granaries.

sentences.zh: 初立之日，准所領中下戶口數，得支一年之糧，逐當州穀價賤時，斟量割當年義租充入。

translations.literal: On the day first established, according to the middle and lower household count under jurisdiction, enough for one year's grain was allotted; when local grain prices were low that year, charity rent of that year was assessed and paid in.
translations.idiomatic: When first established, according to middle and lower household counts under jurisdiction, enough for one year's grain was allotted; when local grain prices were low, that year's charity rent was assessed and deposited.

sentences.zh: 穀貴，下價糶之；

translations.literal: When grain was expensive, sold at low price;
translations.idiomatic: When grain was expensive, it was sold at low price;

sentences.zh: 賤則還用所糶之物，依價糴貯。

translations.literal: When cheap, then used what had been sold and purchased and stored according to price.
translations.idiomatic: When cheap, proceeds from sales were used to purchase and store grain at market price.

sentences.zh: 每歲春月，各依鄉土早晚，課人農桑。

translations.literal: Every year in spring, according to each region's early or late season, people were assigned to agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Every spring, according to each region's season, people were assigned to farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: [6]自春及秋，男十五已上，皆布田畝。

translations.literal: [Note: '入' should read '人' (people); corrected per Cefu 495 and Tongdian 2.] From spring through autumn, males fifteen and above all patrolled the fields by the mu.
translations.idiomatic: [Note: 'enter' should read 'people'; corrected per the Cefu and Tongdian.] From spring through autumn, males fifteen and above all inspected the fields.

sentences.zh: 桑蠶之月，婦女十五已上，皆營蠶桑。

translations.literal: In the mulberry and silkworm month, women fifteen and above all tended mulberry and silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: In the mulberry and silkworm month, women fifteen and above all tended mulberry and silkworms.

sentences.zh: 孟冬，刺史聽審邦教之優劣，定殿最之科品。

translations.literal: In the first month of winter, prefects heard and examined the superiority or inferiority of local instruction and fixed grades of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of winter, prefects reviewed the quality of local instruction and fixed grades of achievement.

sentences.zh: 人有人力無牛，或有牛無力者，須令相便，皆得納種。

translations.literal: If people had human strength but no ox, or had ox but no strength, they had to assist one another; all could pay seed grain.
translations.idiomatic: If people had labor but no ox, or ox but no labor, they had to assist one another; all could contribute seed grain.

sentences.zh: 使地無遺利，人無遊手焉。

translations.literal: Thus land had no wasted benefit and people no idle hands.
translations.idiomatic: Thus no land went unused and no hands idle.

sentences.zh: 緣邊城守之地，堪墾食者，皆營屯田，置都使子使以統之。

translations.literal: Along the frontier garrison lands suitable for reclamation and food, all operated garrison farms; chief and sub-agents were placed to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrison lands suitable for reclamation were all turned to garrison farms, with chief and sub-agents placed to command them.

sentences.zh: 一子使當田五十頃，歲終考其所入，以論褒貶。

translations.literal: One sub-agent managed fifty qing of fields; at year's end his intake was examined to determine praise or censure.
translations.idiomatic: One sub-agent managed fifty qing of fields; at year's end intake was examined to determine praise or censure.

sentences.zh: 是時頻歲大水，州郡多遇沉溺，穀價騰踊。

translations.literal: At that time year after year great floods; many provinces and commanderies were submerged; grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: At that time floods struck year after year; many provinces and commanderies were submerged and grain prices soared.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使開倉，從貴價以糶之，而百姓無益，饑饉尤甚。

translations.literal: The court sent envoys to open granaries and sell at high price, yet the common people gained nothing; famine was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to open granaries and sell at high prices, yet the common people gained nothing and famine grew worse.

sentences.zh: 重以疾疫相乘，死者十四五焉。

translations.literal: Added to this epidemic disease compounded; the dead were fourteen or fifteen in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Epidemic disease compounded the disaster; four or five in ten died.

sentences.zh: 至天統中，[7]又毀東宮，造修文、偃武、隆基嬪嬙諸院，起玳瑁樓。

translations.literal: By the Tiantong period, [Note: '大' should read '天'; corrected per Tongdian 5] again destroyed the Eastern Palace, built the Xiuyang, Yanwu, Longji, and Pinqiang courtyards, and raised the Tortoiseshell Tower.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tiantong period—[Note: 'great' should read 'heaven'; corrected per the Tongdian]—the Eastern Palace was destroyed again and the Xiuyang, Yanwu, Longji, and Pinqiang courtyards built, along with the Tortoiseshell Tower.

sentences.zh: 又於遊豫園穿池，周以列館，中起三山，構臺，以象滄海，并大修佛寺，勞役鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Also in the Youyu Garden a pond was dug, surrounded by rows of lodges; in the center three mountains were raised and terraces built to imitate the blue sea; Buddhist temples were also greatly repaired; corvée labor numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Youyu Garden a pond was dug surrounded by lodges; three mountains and terraces were raised in the center to imitate the sea; Buddhist temples were also greatly repaired; corvée labor numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 財用不給，乃減朝士之祿，斷諸曹糧膳，及九州軍人常賜以供之。

translations.literal: Funds were insufficient; then court officials' salaries were reduced, all bureaus' grain meals cut, and the Nine Provinces' soldiers' regular grants were used to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Funds ran short; court officials' salaries were reduced, bureau grain meals cut, and the Nine Provinces' soldiers' regular grants diverted to supply them.

sentences.zh: 武平之後，權幸並進，賜與無限，加之旱蝗，國用轉屈。

translations.literal: After Wuping, favorites advanced together; grants had no limit; added to drought and locusts, state use turned constrained.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuping, favorites advanced together and grants had no limit; drought and locusts compounded the strain and state revenue tightened.

sentences.zh: 乃料境內六等富人，調令出錢。

translations.literal: Then the six grades of wealthy people within the borders were assessed and ordered to pay money.
translations.idiomatic: Then wealthy people in six grades within the borders were assessed and ordered to pay money.

sentences.zh: 而給事黃門侍郎顏之推奏請立關市邸店之稅，開府鄧長顒贊成之，後主大悅。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yan Zhitui memorialized requesting establishment of market and inn taxes; Grand Master of the Palace Deng Changyuan approved; the Later Lord was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yan Zhitui memorialized requesting market and inn taxes; Grand Master of the Palace Deng Changyuan approved; the Later Lord was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 於是以其所入，以供御府聲色之費，軍國之用不豫焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon its intake supplied the inner palace's music and beauty expenses; military and state use was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon its revenue supplied the inner palace's music and beauty expenses; military and state needs were excluded.

sentences.zh: 未幾而亡。

translations.literal: Before long it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 後周太祖作相，創制六官。

translations.literal: Later Zhou's Taizu as Chancellor created the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou's Taizu, while serving as Chancellor, created the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 載師掌任土之法，辨夫家田里之數，會六畜車乘之稽，審賦役斂弛之節，制畿疆修廣之域，頒施惠之要，審牧產之政。

translations.literal: The Director of Lands managed methods of assigning soil, distinguished numbers of husbands, households, fields, and hamlets, totaled reckoning of six livestock, carts, and chariots, examined the nodes of levies, corvée, collection, and relaxation, regulated the inner and outer domains' cultivated and extended territories, and promulgated essentials of bestowing favor and examined policies of pastoral production.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Lands oversaw methods of assigning soil, counted households, fields, and hamlets, totaled livestock and vehicles, regulated levies and corvée, defined the inner and outer domains, and promulgated policies of favor and pastoral production.

sentences.zh: 司均掌田里之政令。

translations.literal: The Director of Equalization managed policies of fields and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Equalization oversaw policies of fields and hamlets.

sentences.zh: 凡人口十已上，宅五畝；

translations.literal: Generally for population ten and above, five mu of dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: Generally for households of ten or more, five mu of dwelling;

sentences.zh: 口九已上，[8]宅四畝；

translations.literal: Population nine and above, [Note: should read 'nine and below' to connect with 'five and below' below] four mu of dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: Households of nine or more—[Note: text should read 'nine and below' to connect with the following clause]—four mu of dwelling;

sentences.zh: 口五已下，宅三畝。

translations.literal: Population five and below, three mu of dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Households of five or below, three mu of dwelling.

sentences.zh: 有室者，田百四十畝，丁者田百畝。

translations.literal: Those with wives received one hundred forty mu of fields; adult laborers one hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: Households with wives received one hundred forty mu of fields; adult laborers one hundred mu.

sentences.zh: 司賦掌功賦之政令。

translations.literal: The Director of Levies managed policies of labor levies.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Levies oversaw policies of labor levies.

sentences.zh: 凡人自十八以至六十有四，與輕癃者，皆賦之。

translations.literal: Generally all people from eighteen to sixty-four, and the lightly disabled, all paid levies.
translations.idiomatic: Generally all people from eighteen to sixty-four, and the lightly disabled, paid levies.

sentences.zh: 其賦之法，有室者，歲不過絹一疋，綿八兩，粟五斛；

translations.literal: The method of levies: those with wives, each year not exceeding one bolt of silk, eight liang of cotton, five hu of millet;
translations.idiomatic: The levy method: households with wives paid each year no more than one bolt of silk, eight liang of cotton, and five hu of millet;

sentences.zh: 丁者半之。

translations.literal: Adult laborers paid half.
translations.idiomatic: Adult laborers paid half.

sentences.zh: 其非桑土，有室者，布一疋，麻十斤；

translations.literal: Where not mulberry soil, those with wives: one bolt of cloth, ten jin of hemp;
translations.idiomatic: Where soil was not suited to mulberry, households with wives paid one bolt of cloth and ten jin of hemp;

sentences.zh: 丁者又半之。

translations.literal: Adult laborers again half.
translations.idiomatic: Adult laborers again paid half.

sentences.zh: 豐年則全賦，中年半之，下年一之，皆以時徵焉。

translations.literal: Abundant years paid full levy, moderate years half, poor years one part in ten—all collected according to season.
translations.idiomatic: In abundant years the full levy was paid, in moderate years half, in poor years one part in ten—all collected according to season.

sentences.zh: 若艱凶札，則不徵其賦。

translations.literal: If hardship and pestilence, then levies were not collected.
translations.idiomatic: In hardship and pestilence, levies were not collected.

sentences.zh: 司役掌力役之政令。

translations.literal: The Director of Corvée managed policies of labor corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Corvée oversaw policies of labor corvée.

sentences.zh: 凡人自十八以至五十有九，皆任於役。

translations.literal: Generally all people from eighteen to fifty-nine all bore corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Generally all people from eighteen to fifty-nine bore corvée.

sentences.zh: 豐年不過三旬，中年則二旬，下年則一旬。

translations.literal: Abundant years not exceeding thirty days, moderate years twenty days, poor years ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In abundant years corvée did not exceed thirty days, in moderate years twenty, in poor years ten.

sentences.zh: 凡起徒役，無過家一人。

translations.literal: Generally when raising corvée labor, no more than one person per household.
translations.idiomatic: When raising corvée labor, no household contributed more than one person.

sentences.zh: 其人有年八十者，一子不從役，百年者，家不從役。

translations.literal: If a person was eighty, one son did not serve corvée; if a hundred, the household did not serve corvée.
translations.idiomatic: If a person was eighty, one son was exempt from corvée; if a hundred, the whole household was exempt.

sentences.zh: 廢疾非人不養者，一人不從役。

translations.literal: The severely disabled with no one to support them—one person did not serve corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The severely disabled with no one to support them—one person was exempt from corvée.

sentences.zh: 若凶札，又無力征。

translations.literal: If famine and pestilence, again no labor was levied.
translations.idiomatic: In famine and pestilence, no labor was levied.

sentences.zh: 掌鹽掌四鹽之政令。

translations.literal: The Salt Director managed policies of the four salts.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt Director oversaw policies of the four salts.

sentences.zh: 一曰散鹽，煑海以成之；

translations.literal: First, loose salt—boiling the sea to make it;
translations.idiomatic: First, loose salt—made by boiling seawater;

sentences.zh: 二曰盬鹽，引池以化之；

translations.literal: Second, brine salt—drawing pools to transform it;
translations.idiomatic: Second, brine salt—made by drawing brine pools;

sentences.zh: 三曰形鹽，物地以出之；

translations.literal: Third, shape salt—produced from the earth;
translations.idiomatic: Third, shape salt—produced from the earth;

sentences.zh: 四曰飴鹽，於戎以取之。

translations.literal: Fourth, sweet salt—obtained from the Rong frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, sweet salt—obtained from the frontier Rong.

sentences.zh: 凡盬鹽形鹽，每地為之禁，百姓取之，皆稅焉。

translations.literal: Generally for brine salt and shape salt, each place had its prohibition; common people who took it all paid tax.
translations.idiomatic: For brine salt and shape salt, each region had its monopoly; common people who took it all paid tax.

sentences.zh: 司倉掌辨九穀之物，以量國用。

translations.literal: The Granary Director managed distinguishing the nine grains to measure state use.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Director distinguished the nine grains to measure state consumption.

sentences.zh: 國用足，即蓄其餘，以待凶荒；

translations.literal: When state use was sufficient, the remainder was stored against flood and famine;
translations.idiomatic: When state needs were met, the remainder was stored against flood and famine;

sentences.zh: 不足則止。

translations.literal: When insufficient, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When insufficient, collection stopped.

sentences.zh: 餘用足，則以粟貸人。

translations.literal: When surplus was sufficient, grain was lent to people.
translations.idiomatic: When surplus was sufficient, grain was lent to the people.

sentences.zh: 春頒之，秋斂之。

translations.literal: Distributed in spring, collected in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Distributed in spring, collected in autumn.

sentences.zh: 閔帝元年，初除市門稅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Min, market gate tax was first abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Min's first year, market gate tax was first abolished.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝即位，復興入市之稅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, market-entry tax was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, market-entry tax was restored.

sentences.zh: 武帝保定元年，改八丁兵為十二丁兵，率歲一月役。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding of Emperor Wu, eight-adult-soldier corvée was changed to twelve-adult-soldier corvée, generally one month of corvée per year.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu's Baoding year 1, the eight-adult-soldier corvée was changed to twelve-adult-soldier corvée, generally one month of corvée per year.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，改軍士為侍官，募百姓充之，除其縣籍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, garrison soldiers were changed to attendant officials; common people were recruited to fill them and removed from county registration.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2, garrison soldiers became attendant officials; common people were recruited to fill the ranks and removed from county registration.

sentences.zh: 是後夏人半為兵矣。

translations.literal: From this half the people of Xia became soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: From this half the people of the realm became soldiers.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，發山東諸州，增一月功為四十五日役，以起洛陽宮。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuan's time, the eastern Shandong provinces were mobilized; one month of labor was increased to forty-five days of corvée to build the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan, the eastern Shandong provinces were mobilized; one month of labor was increased to forty-five days of corvée to build the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 并移相州六府於洛陽，稱東京六府。

translations.literal: Also moved the six offices of Xiangzhou to Luoyang, called the Eastern Capital Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The six offices of Xiangzhou were also moved to Luoyang, called the Eastern Capital Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 武帝保定二年正月，初於蒲州開河渠，同州開龍首渠，以廣溉灌。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Baoding of Emperor Wu, at first the river canal at Puzhou and Longshou Canal at Tongzhou were opened to expand irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu's Baoding year 2, first month, the river canal at Puzhou and Longshou Canal at Tongzhou were opened to expand irrigation.

sentences.zh: 高祖登庸，罷東京之役，除入市之稅。

translations.literal: When Gaozu assumed power, Eastern Capital corvée was abolished and market-entry tax removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu assumed power, Eastern Capital corvée was abolished and market-entry tax removed.

sentences.zh: 是時尉迥、王謙、司馬消難，相次叛逆，興師誅討，賞費鉅萬。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Cong, Wang Qian, and Sima Xiaonan rebelled in succession; armies were raised to suppress them; rewards and expenses numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Cong, Wang Qian, and Sima Xiaonan rebelled in succession; armies were raised to suppress them at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，又遷都，發山東丁，毀造宮室。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the abdication, the capital was again moved; Shandong corvée laborers were mobilized to destroy and build palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Upon receiving the abdication the capital was moved again; Shandong corvée laborers were mobilized to destroy and build palaces.

sentences.zh: 仍依周制，役丁為十二番，匠則六番。

translations.literal: Still following Zhou institutions, corvée laborers had twelve rotations, artisans six.
translations.idiomatic: Still following Zhou institutions, corvée laborers had twelve rotations, artisans six.

sentences.zh: 及頒新令，制人五家為保，保有長。

translations.literal: When the new statutes were promulgated, five households formed a bao, each bao having a chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the new statutes were promulgated, five households formed a bao, each with a chief.

sentences.zh: 保五為閭，閭四為族，皆有正。

translations.literal: Five bao formed a lin, four lin a zu—all had chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Five bao formed a lin, four lin a zu—all with chiefs.

sentences.zh: 畿外置里正，比閭正，黨長比族正，以相檢察焉。

translations.literal: Outside the capital li chiefs were placed, compared to lin chiefs; dang chiefs compared to zu chiefs—to inspect one another.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital li chiefs were placed, equivalent to lin chiefs; dang chiefs equivalent to zu chiefs—to inspect one another.

sentences.zh: 男女三歲已下為黃，十歲已下為小，十七已下為中，十八已上為丁。
