translations.idiomatic: ' Before long the emperor died; Six Zhu was abolished and Five Zhu circulated.

sentences.zh: 竟至陳亡。

translations.literal: Ultimately until Chen's fall.
translations.idiomatic: This continued until Chen's fall.

sentences.zh: 其嶺南諸州，多以鹽米布交易，俱不用錢云。

translations.literal: Those southern mountain passes' various provinces mostly used salt, rice, and cloth for trade—all did not use coin.
translations.idiomatic: Southern frontier provinces mostly used salt, rice, and cloth for trade—all without coin.

sentences.zh: 齊神武霸政之初，承魏猶用永安五銖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Shenwu's hegemonic governance, inheriting Wei still used Yong'an Five Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Gao Huan's hegemonic governance, Wei still used Yong'an Five Zhu.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴已後，百姓私鑄，體制漸別，遂各以為名。

translations.literal: After moving to Ye, common people privately cast; form gradually differed; then each had its own name.
translations.idiomatic: After moving to Ye, people privately cast coin; forms gradually differed; each region had its own name.

sentences.zh: 有雍州青赤，梁州生厚、緊錢、吉錢，河陽生澀、天柱、赤牽之稱。

translations.literal: There were Yong Province green-red, Liang Province raw-thick, tight coin, Ji coin; Heyang raw-rough, Tianzhu, Red-Qian names.
translations.idiomatic: There were Yong Province green-red, Liang Province raw-thick, tight coin, and Ji coin; Heyang raw-rough, Tianzhu, and Red-Qian names.

sentences.zh: 冀州之北，錢皆不行，交貿者皆以絹布。

translations.literal: North of Ji Province coin all did not circulate; traders all used silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: North of Ji Province coin did not circulate; traders all used silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 神武帝乃收境內之銅及錢，仍依舊文更鑄，流之四境。

translations.literal: Shenwu then collected copper and coin within the borders; still according to old inscription newly cast, flowing to the four borders.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan collected copper and coin within the borders and recast according to the old inscription, flowing to the four borders.

sentences.zh: 未幾之間，漸復細薄，姦偽競起。

translations.literal: Before long between, gradually again thin and light; fraud and falsity competed to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Before long coin again grew thin and light; fraud competed to arise.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，除永安之錢，改鑄常平五銖，重如其文。

translations.literal: Wenxuan received the abdication; abolished Yong'an coin; changed cast to Ever-Normal Five Zhu, weight matching inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan received the abdication; abolished Yong'an coin and cast Ever-Normal Five Zhu, weight matching inscription.

sentences.zh: 其錢甚貴，且制造甚精。

translations.literal: The coin was very valuable and manufacture very refined.
translations.idiomatic: The coin was very valuable and manufacture very refined.

sentences.zh: 至乾明、皇建之間，往往私鑄。

translations.literal: By Qianming and Huangjian periods, often privately cast.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qianming and Huangjian periods, private casting was common.

sentences.zh: 鄴中用錢，有赤熟、青熟、細眉、赤生之異。

translations.literal: Coin used in Ye had red-ripe, green-ripe, fine-brow, red-raw differences.
translations.idiomatic: Coin used in Ye had red-ripe, green-ripe, fine-brow, and red-raw varieties.

sentences.zh: 河南所用，有青薄鉛錫之別。

translations.literal: Henan used had green-thin, lead-tin differences.
translations.idiomatic: Henan used green-thin and lead-tin varieties.

sentences.zh: 青、齊、徐、兗、梁、豫州，輩類各殊。

translations.literal: Qing, Qi, Xu, Yan, Liang, Yu provinces—types each differed.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, Qi, Xu, Yan, Liang, and Yu provinces—types each differed.

sentences.zh: 武平已後，私鑄轉甚，或以生鐵和銅。

translations.literal: After Wuping, private casting turned increasingly severe; some mixed raw iron with copper.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuping, private casting grew severe; some mixed raw iron with copper.

sentences.zh: 至于齊亡，卒不能禁。

translations.literal: Until Qi's fall, ultimately could not be prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Until Qi's fall, it ultimately could not be prohibited.

sentences.zh: 高祖既受周禪，以天下錢貨輕重不等，乃更鑄新錢。

translations.literal: Gaozu having received Zhou's abdication, because realm coin was light and heavy unequal, then newly cast new coin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu having received Zhou's abdication, because realm coin varied in weight, newly cast standard coin.

sentences.zh: 背面肉好，皆有周郭，文曰「五銖」，而重如其文。

translations.literal: Obverse and reverse rim and hole all had complete rim; inscription 'Five Zhu,' weight matching inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Obverse and reverse rim and hole all had complete rims; inscribed 'Five Zhu,' weight matching inscription.

sentences.zh: 每錢一千，重四斤二兩。

translations.literal: Each thousand coins weighed four jin two liang.
translations.idiomatic: Each thousand coins weighed four jin two liang.

sentences.zh: 是時錢既新出，百姓或私有鎔鑄。

translations.literal: At that time coin newly issued; common people sometimes privately melted and cast.
translations.idiomatic: When coin was newly issued, people sometimes privately melted and cast.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，詔四面諸關，各付百錢為樣。

translations.literal: Third year fourth month edict: four-side passes each given one hundred coins as sample.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3, fourth month edict: four-side passes each given one hundred coins as sample.

sentences.zh: 從關外來，勘樣相似，然後得過。

translations.literal: Coming from outside the pass, examining sample for similarity, then permitted to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Coming from outside the pass, if the sample matched, passage was permitted.

sentences.zh: 樣不同者，即壞以為銅，入官。

translations.literal: Where sample differed, then destroyed as copper, entered office.
translations.idiomatic: Where the sample differed, coin was destroyed for copper and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 詔行新錢已後，前代舊錢，有五行大布、永通萬國及齊常平，所在用以貿易不止。

translations.literal: Edict after new coin circulated, former dynasty old coin—Wuxing Dabo, Yontong Wanguo, and Qi Ever-Normal—everywhere used for trade without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: After the new coin circulated, former dynasty old coin—Wuxing Dabo, Yontong Wanguo, and Qi Ever-Normal—continued in trade everywhere.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔仍依舊不禁者，縣令奪半年祿。

translations.literal: Fourth year edict: those still not prohibited—magistrates deprived half-year salary.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4 edict: where still not prohibited, magistrates lost half a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 然百姓習用既久，尚猶不絕。

translations.literal: Yet common people accustomed to use long, still not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people long accustomed to old coin still did not cease.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，詔又嚴其制。

translations.literal: Fifth year first month edict again strictened the system.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, first month edict again strictened the system.

sentences.zh: 自是錢貨始一，所在流布，百姓便之。

translations.literal: From this coin currency first unified; everywhere circulated; common people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: From this coin was first unified; it circulated everywhere and people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 是時見用之錢，皆須和以錫鑞。

translations.literal: At that time coin in use all had to be mixed with tin and lead.
translations.idiomatic: Coin in use all had to be mixed with tin and lead.

sentences.zh: 錫鑞既賤，求利者多，私鑄之錢，不可禁約。

translations.literal: Tin and lead being cheap, profit-seekers many; privately cast coin could not be prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Tin and lead being cheap, profit-seekers were many; private casting could not be prohibited.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔乃禁出錫鑞之處，並不得私有採取。

translations.literal: That year edict prohibited tin and lead mining places—none permitted private extraction.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict prohibited private extraction at tin and lead mining places.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔晉王廣，聽於揚州立五鑪鑄錢。

translations.literal: Tenth year edict Prince of Jin Guang permitted to establish five furnaces casting coin at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10 edict permitted Prince of Jin Yang Guang to establish five furnaces casting coin at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後姦狡稍漸磨鑢錢郭，取銅私鑄，又雜以錫錢，遞相放效，錢遂輕薄。

translations.literal: Afterward the crafty gradually ground and filed coin rims, took copper for private casting; also mixed tin coin; mutually imitating—coin then light and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the crafty gradually filed coin rims and took copper for private casting; also mixed tin coin; coin grew light and thin.

sentences.zh: 乃下惡錢之禁。

translations.literal: Then issued prohibition of bad coin.
translations.idiomatic: Then prohibition of bad coin was issued.

sentences.zh: 京師及諸州邸肆之上，皆令立榜，置樣為准。

translations.literal: Capital and all provinces' market inns above all ordered to erect placards, placing samples as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and all provinces' market inns were ordered to erect placards with samples as standard.

sentences.zh: 不中樣者，不入於市。

translations.literal: Those not matching sample did not enter the market.
translations.idiomatic: Coin not matching the sample did not enter the market.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔漢王諒，聽於并州立五鑢鑄錢。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year edict Prince of Han Liang permitted to establish five furnaces casting coin at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18 edict permitted Prince of Han Yang Liang to establish five furnaces casting coin at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時江南人間錢少，晉王廣又聽於鄂州白紵山有銅𨥥處，錮銅鑄錢。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangnan among the people coin was few; Prince of Jin Guang again permitted at Ezhou Baiyu Mountain copper mine place to imprison copper and cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had little coin; Prince of Jin Yang Guang again permitted imprisoning copper at Ezhou Baiyu Mountain to cast coin.

sentences.zh: 於是詔聽置十鑪鑄錢。

translations.literal: Thereupon edict permitted establishing ten furnaces casting coin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted establishing ten furnaces casting coin.

sentences.zh: 又詔蜀王秀，聽於益州立五鑪鑄錢。

translations.literal: Also edict Prince of Shu Xiu permitted to establish five furnaces casting coin at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Yang Xiu was also permitted to establish five furnaces casting coin at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 是時錢益濫惡，乃令有司，括天下邸肆見錢，非官鑄者，皆毀之，其銅入官。

translations.literal: At that time coin increasingly debased; then ordered responsible offices to inventory all realm market inn visible coin—not officially cast—all destroyed; copper entered office.
translations.idiomatic: Coin grew increasingly debased; responsible offices were ordered to inventory all market coin—not officially cast—all destroyed and copper confiscated.

sentences.zh: 而京師以惡錢貿易，為吏所執，有死者。

translations.literal: Yet capital because bad coin trade, caught by officials, some died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the capital some died when caught trading bad coin.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，私鑄頗息。

translations.literal: Within several years private casting somewhat ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years private casting somewhat ceased.

sentences.zh: 大業已後，王綱弛紊，巨姦大猾，遂多私鑄，錢轉薄惡。

translations.literal: After Daye, royal net slackened and disordered; great villains and great scoundrels then many privately cast; coin turned thin and bad.
translations.idiomatic: After Daye, governance slackened; great scoundrels privately cast coin ever more; coin turned thin and bad.

sentences.zh: 初每千猶重二斤，後漸輕至一斤。

translations.literal: At first each thousand still weighed two jin; afterward gradually light to one jin.
translations.idiomatic: At first each thousand still weighed two jin; afterward gradually lightened to one jin.

sentences.zh: 或翦鐵鍱，裁皮糊紙以為錢，相雜用之。

translations.literal: Some cut iron sheets, trimmed leather pasted paper to make coin, mixed for use.
translations.idiomatic: Some cut iron sheets or trimmed leather pasted with paper to make coin, mixed for use.

sentences.zh: 貨賤物貴，以至於亡。

translations.literal: Goods cheap and things expensive, reaching to perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Goods grew cheap and prices expensive, reaching collapse.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 道關政亂 「政」當作「治」，唐人諱改。

translations.literal: Dao guan zheng luan: 'zheng' should read 'zhi'; Tang people changed it due to taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Dao guan zheng luan: 'zheng' (governance) should read 'zhi' (order and disorder); altered under Tang dynastic taboo.

sentences.zh: 准所輸 通典五，「准」作「惟」。

translations.literal: Zhun suo shu: Tongdian 5 reads 'zhun' as 'wei'.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun suo shu: the Tongdian, book 5, reads 'zhun' (according to) as 'wei' (only).

sentences.zh: 不可委載 「委」原作「妄」，據通典三五改。

translations.literal: Bu ke wei zai: 'wei' originally read 'wang'; corrected according to Tongdian 35.
translations.idiomatic: Bu ke wei zai: 'wei' (wrongly) originally read 'wang' (wildly); corrected according to Tongdian 35.

sentences.zh: 永業田 原作「永田」，據冊府四九五、通典二改。

translations.literal: Yongye tian: original read 'yong tian'; corrected according to Cefu 495 and Tongdian 2.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye tian (perpetual fields): original read 'yong tian'; corrected according to Cefu 495 and Tongdian 2.

sentences.zh: 限止四牛 「牛」原作「年」，據通典二改。

translations.literal: Xian zhi si niu: 'niu' (oxen) originally read 'nian' (year); corrected according to Tongdian 2.
translations.idiomatic: Xian zhi si niu (limited to four oxen): 'niu' originally read 'nian' (year); corrected according to Tongdian 2.

sentences.zh: 課人農桑 「人」原作「入」，據冊府四九五、通典二改。

translations.literal: Ke ren nong sang: 'ren' (people) originally read 'ru' (enter); corrected according to Cefu 495 and Tongdian 2.
translations.idiomatic: Ke ren nong sang (assign people to farming and sericulture): 'ren' originally read 'ru' (enter); corrected according to Cefu 495 and Tongdian 2.

sentences.zh: 至天統中 「天」原作「大」，據通典五改。

translations.literal: Zhi tian tong zhong: 'tian' (heaven) originally read 'da' (great); corrected according to Tongdian 5.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi tian tong zhong (by the Tiantong period): 'tian' originally read 'da' (great); corrected according to Tongdian 5.

sentences.zh: 口九已上 按：應作「口九已下」，才能和下文「口五已下」相銜接。

translations.literal: Kou jiu yi shang: Note: should read 'kou jiu yi xia' (nine and below) to connect with 'kou wu yi xia' (five and below) below.
translations.idiomatic: Kou jiu yi shang (population nine and above): Note: should read 'nine and below' to connect with 'five and below' below.

sentences.zh: 朱雀門 本書高祖紀下作「廣陽門」。

translations.literal: Zhuque men: This book's Annals of Gaozu, lower, reads 'Guangyang Gate'.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuque Gate: the Annals of Gaozu, lower, read 'Guangyang Gate' instead.

sentences.zh: 前後用穀五百餘石 陸錫熊炳爥偶鈔：按文當作「五百餘萬石」，疑脫「萬」字。

translations.literal: Qian hou yong gu wu bai yu shi: Lu Xixiong and Bing Juer's Collation Notes: According to the text it should read 'five million-plus shi'; suspect missing character 'wan' (ten thousand).
translations.idiomatic: Qian hou yong gu wu bai yu shi (before and after used more than five hundred shi of grain): Lu Xixiong and Bing Juer's Collation Notes: the text should read 'five million-plus shi'; the character 'ten thousand' is likely missing.

sentences.zh: 慕容佛允 本書吐谷渾傳，「佛」作「伏」，音譯異字。

translations.literal: Murong Fo Yun: This book's Tuyuhun Biography reads 'Fu' for 'Fo'—transliteration variant characters.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Fuyun: the Tuyuhun Biography reads a different character for the second syllable—transliteration variant.
